climateNote: This is a tectonic event: coseismic rupture on the East Anatolian Fault. No climate connection is claimed — it is included for the single-pass-pair rupture signature and the L-band vs C-band comparison.

dataset.mission: Sentinel-1A/B (Copernicus), ascending pass, single pass pair spanning the rupture
dataset.datasetId: USGS event page 2023 Kahramanmaraş M 7.8; Copernicus Sentinel-1 SLC
dataset.window: Published: 6 February 2023 rupture; in-app pass pair: 12 days with coseismic step at day 6
dataset.coverage: East Anatolian Fault — ~300 km rupture, Pazarcık segment (~380 km scene)
dataset.gnss: No bundled GNSS chart — coseismic offsets are step functions; published GNSS/InSAR coseismic studies are cited instead
dataset.processing: Published: USGS rupture characterization, published InSAR coseismic maps. In-app: elastic rectangular rupture (5 m slip at 15 km depth); one fringe = λ/2 line-of-sight motion

items.label: MEASURED
items.detail: M 7.8 on 6 Feb 2023, East Anatolian Fault, ~300 km surface rupture (USGS). Shown as citations; not re-derived in-app.

items.label: MODELED
items.detail: Physics rendering of a rectangular rupture (5 m slip, 300 km length). NOT a raw SAR image — computed on-device.

items.label: DERIVED
items.detail: Computed on-device from the physical model (one fringe = λ/2 LOS). Tracks the model, not a downloaded product.

items.label: LIVE
items.detail: Live accelerometer from the demo ESP32 ground station — IoT demo at the demo site; not a satellite measurement of this event.

limitations: The interferogram is a physics rendering of published figures, not raw SAR pixels — no SAR processing is done in-app.
A single uniform-slip rectangle cannot reproduce the multi-segment, M 7.5 doublet complexity.
Near-fault signal loss (decorrelation) visible in real coseismic scenes is not simulated in-app.

sources.title: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program — M 7.8 Türkiye earthquake, 6 February 2023
